meta.comment: engine.traffic (planned MOD) inc0 table (b): trip-generation rates per person and per land-use class, plus freight tonnes/job/day by sector. Demand is generated from PEOPLE (residents + in-city workers), not from buildings -- a building only matters as the land-use class that determines how many of its occupants' trips ATTRACT to it (Aaron's brief: 'traffic is ALL transportation for what is built', but the demand SOURCE is residents plus people who work there).
meta.unitsConvention: tripRatePersonPerDay is person-trips/person/day (a one-way journey, matches scale_ladder.json); freightTonnesPerJobPerDay is metric tonnes/job/day, sector-attributed (matches data/freight.json's tonnes/day unit convention, referenced not restated).

residentTripRate.note: Resident-side all-purpose trip rate is density-varying, not a single constant -- see scale_ladder.json's per-rung tripRatePersonPerDay (table k) and its source anchors (UK DfT NTS0409, Tokyo Person Trip Survey). This block exists to document the SHAPE, not restate the numbers: near-flat 2.3-2.9 trips/person/day band, gently rising through small/medium settlements (more discretionary trip-chaining as services densify) and easing back toward the ~2.4-2.5 Tokyo-anchor figure at megacity scale (time-budget and congestion self-limiting effects, HCM 2010 Ch.16 discussion of trip suppression under sustained high v/c).
residentTripRate.source: UK DfT National Travel Survey NTS0409 (trip rate by area type); Tokyo Metropolitan Area Person Trip Survey (5th round, MLIT/TMG)

commuteLegsPerWorkerPerDay.note: Standard round-trip commute: one outbound + one return leg per working day, per worker physically working in the city (residentWorker or in-commuter). Does not include discretionary trips made ON a workday, which are covered by residentTripRate.
commuteLegsPerWorkerPerDay.source: Structural definition (a commute is a return journey); UK NTS commute-leg convention.

workerTripRate.note: workersInCity (scale_ladder.json per-rung field) x commuteLegsPerWorkerPerDay gives the commute-only trip component; this is a SUBSET of dailyPersonTrips (residents already include their own commute trips in residentTripRate), not an additive total. In-commuters (people who live outside the city but work inside it, MOD-035 external commuting) contribute commuteLegsPerWorkerPerDay trips each but zero residentTripRate trips -- they appear only as commute legs plus whatever discretionary trips they make while in the city (approximated at 0.3 extra legs/day, placeholder, for lunch/shopping-while-at-work).

tripsPerVehiclePerDay.$comment: FEAT-2326609800 inc7 (AC-3, ASM-1532): trips made PER VEHICLE per day, by road/freight vehicle class -- the divisor that turns a class's daily vehicle-trips (trafficAssignment.ts assignedFlowByClassOf) into an implied vehicles-owned count for Road Tax (VED), since no per-citizen vehicle-ownership state exists in the engine today (D1). Directional placeholders, order-of-magnitude UK NTS/DfT vehicle-utilisation figures -- higher-utilisation commercial classes (taxi, bus, freight) make many more trips/day per vehicle than a privately-owned car, so the SAME daily vehicle-trip total implies far FEWER owned vehicles for those classes.

car.source: UK NTS: one return commute/errand journey per vehicle per day is the modal private-car pattern (matches trip_generation.json's own commuteLegsPerWorkerPerDay=2.0 structural anchor above)

motorbike.source: as car -- privately owned, similar usage pattern

taxi.source: derived approximation, UK PHV/taxi fleet order-of-magnitude (a taxi is in near-continuous fare service across a working day, unlike a privately-owned car)

bus.source: derived approximation, UK PSV bus fleet order-of-magnitude (multiple scheduled round trips per vehicle per operating day)

cargo_van.source: derived approximation, UK LGV delivery-round order-of-magnitude (several multi-drop rounds per vehicle per day)

rigid_truck.source: derived approximation, UK HGV rigid distribution-round order-of-magnitude

articulated_truck.source: derived approximation, UK HGV articulated long-haul order-of-magnitude (fewer, longer trips per vehicle per day than a rigid distribution truck)

landUseTripRates.$comment: Trip ATTRACTION rates per unit of land-use, for consumers of this table who need to distribute city-wide generated trips across destination buildings (a downstream inc2 concern; provided now so inc0 is complete per the BOW brief's list). Units: trips attracted per day per the stated denominator. Directional placeholders informed by UK TRICS-style trip-generation orders of magnitude (TRICS is a commercial database; these are NOT TRICS-licensed figures, they are independently-derived sanity-checked approximations -- confidence: derived, not measured).

dwelling_low_density.source: derived approximation, UK trip-generation literature order-of-magnitude

dwelling_high_density.source: derived approximation (denser dwellings show lower per-unit car-trip generation, higher walk/transit share captured elsewhere in mode share, not trip count)

retail_job.source: derived approximation (retail attracts customer trips beyond staff commute)

hospital_bed.source: derived approximation (staff shifts + visitors + patient transport)

stadium_seat.unit: per seat, averaged over a full year (event days spike far higher, event-day multiplier is an inc2+ concern)

airport_job.source: derived approximation; airport PASSENGER trips are a separate, much larger figure already governed by data/airport.json's paxPerRunwayPerDay/paxPerGatePerDay (referenced, not restated) -- this row covers airport STAFF commute only

freightTonnesPerJobPerDay.$comment: Sector-level freight intensity used by scale_ladder.json's freightTonnesBySector derivation. Sector ids are this table's own taxonomy (a coarser grouping than data/freight.json's 5 production chains), chosen to map cleanly onto data/naming/attract sector concepts without duplicating freight.json's own chain-stage tonnesPerDay figures (GR#3 -- those are PRODUCTION rates for specific chain stages; these are city-wide freight-MOVEMENT intensity per worker in a sector, a different denominator).

construction.source: derived approximation, informed by data/freight.json construction-chain jobs:output ratios as an order-of-magnitude cross-check, independently re-derived per worker (not copied)

manufacturing.source: derived approximation, informed by data/freight.json steelAndMachinery-chain jobs:output ratios as a cross-check

food.source: derived approximation, informed by data/freight.json food-chain jobs:output ratios as a cross-check

logistics_retail.source: derived approximation (distribution-heavy sector, higher tonnes/job than production sectors)

services_office.source: derived approximation (parcels/consumables only, negligible bulk freight)

sectorMixByDensityBand.$comment: City-wide worker sector mix by density band (fractions sum to 1.0 per band), feeding scale_ladder.json's freightTonnesBySector. Reflects standard structural change: primary/construction-heavy at low density, services-dominant at megacity scale (a well-established urbanisation pattern, not a specific cited dataset -- confidence: derived).

provenance.source: See per-block source fields above; composite of UK DfT NTS, Tokyo Person Trip Survey, and derived structural-economics approximations
provenance.note: No figure in this file is a directly measured, single-cited number -- every row is either a documented survey-anchored SHAPE (residentTripRate) or an internally-consistent derived approximation used only to exercise the scale_ladder.json rollup. Flagged for Aaron's balance pass same as every other v1 Metropolis data table.
